subject: Routing containment & model commitment for HealthPilot — risk/rollout plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Routing containment & model commitment for HealthPilot — risk/rollout plan

Team — quick background: HealthPilot (external contact Aisha) has asked us for a strict routing containment: all inference for their prod workspace must run in us-west-2, and they want an explicit model commitment (single model family, no automatic fallback to lower-cost variants). This is driven by their internal regulator and procurement; they will sign only if we can guarantee containment + model commitment for the first 18 months.

Asks for this thread:
- Confirm feasibility and list technical risks (Karthik)
- Product guidance on what exactly we can commit to (Marissa) — model family/version policy, fallback semantics
- Legal / sales constraints we need to surface to customer (Lauren)
- Ops/infra cost and capacity implications (Monica)

Initial proposal (30m read):
1) Per-customer routing rule that pins HealthPilot to us-west-2 for prod.
2) A "model commitment" SKU: locked to a specific model family + quantization profile; no automatic fallback to cheaper/heterogeneous variants. We allow controlled manual rollback with customer-notified maintenance windows.
3) Capacity reservation on dedicated pool (soft-reserve + burst) to meet their SLA; circuit-breaker in place to prevent spillover.
4) Runtime safety: enable strict KV cache isolation and disable cross-customer prefix caching for that tenant.

Attached: high-level dataflow + draft playbook.

Please reply with explicit "go / blockers / timeline" by EOD TOMORROW. I want to get a call scheduled with HealthPilot this week if we can present a concrete plan.

— Vivek
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: HealthPilot_DataFlow_Diagram.v1.pdf (diagram), routing_playbook_draft.md (proposal)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Routing containment & model commitment for HealthPilot — risk/rollout plan

Thanks Vivek — high level thumbs up, but a few product clarifications before we promise anything to the customer: 

1) Model commitment scope: do they want a single exact model version (e.g., redwood-v2.1-8k) or a guaranteed family (v2.x) with allowed security patches? We should avoid promising pinning to a single commit SHA without an upgrade policy.
2) Fallback semantics: we can commit to "no automatic fallback" but we need a manual emergency fallback plan (with customer consent) if their reserved capacity is exhausted.
3) SLAs: if they require low 99th latency region-only, that drives different sizing than just "don't route outside region."

If we agree on product language, I can draft the commitment clause for the contract team. Timeline: I can have proposal language and a one-pager by EOD Thursday.

— Marissa
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Routing containment & model commitment for HealthPilot — risk/rollout plan

Technical input / constraints — long version below, TL;DR: doable but non-trivial; expect ~4 sprint lift + capacity reservation costs.

Key technical notes:
- Routing: we already support policy-based routing by tenant; adding a firm "no route outside region" flag is straightforward at the controller layer, but must be enforced in the routing plane and the serving runtime. We need validation tests to prevent accidental policy regressions.
- Model commitment: preventing automatic fallback is mostly a policy change, but we must also ensure the scheduler doesn't place the tenant on nodes that host only compatible but downgraded quantized kernels. In practice that means adding a per-tenant capability vector (allowed kernel profiles).
- Capacity & autoscaler: to meet strict containment + no-fallback, we must reserve capacity in us-west-2. That affects our autoscaler: soft reservation + burst model works, but cost will be higher; there should be an option to move to dedicated pool for large commits.
- Cache isolation and memory: enabling strict KV isolation increases memory pressure; may require higher instance sizes or pinning to fewer requests per GPU.
- Rollout & canary: do a 2-stage canary — internal small traffic, then mirrored traffic from non-prod customer workspace, then customer-scheduled cutover. Documented maintenance window required for any manual rollback.

Open engineering questions:
1) Does the contract need us to preserve exact model weights (binary) for 18 months? If yes, we need retention policy for model artifacts.
2) How strict is their no-fallback requirement during infra incidents? If they insist on 0% routing outside region even under partial outage, we need to model SLO failures and escalation.

I attached a quick table in the playbook draft showing impact by traffic percentile. Estimate: 4 sprints (8 engineers partial), plus ops work to carve out and instrument reservations.

— Karthik
VP, Serving Platform
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Routing containment & model commitment for HealthPilot — risk/rollout plan

Thanks all — summary and next steps from legal/sales perspective: 

1) Contract language: we should avoid language that ties us to a specific commit SHA unless we also add an "upgrade exceptions" schedule. Marissa — please provide the two alternative phrasings (exact-version + upgrades by mutual consent vs. family + allowed patches).
2) Risk acceptance: HealthPilot needs to sign a "service containment addendum" that outlines: reserved capacity costs, expected latency behavior during regional incidents, and an emergency fallback process requiring 24-hour notice and mutual sign-off.
3) Timeline & go/no-go: Agree with Karthik — engineering estimate is ~4 sprints. Sales/Legal can present a conditional proposal to HealthPilot next week that includes an implementation timeline and an interim mitigation (temporary dedicated pool with a provisional SLA).

Action items:
- Marissa: draft commitment clause + one-pager (due 2027-05-20 EOD)
- Karthik: confirm sprint plan and resource ask in JIRA INF-9823 (due 2027-05-21)
- Monica: produce a cost estimate for soft-reserve vs dedicated (due 2027-05-21)
- Vivek: schedule a 30m sync with HealthPilot (Aisha + Carlos) for 2027-05-24; please include product, engineering, and legal.

I'll coordinate with Sales to get a commercial overlay. If there are any non-negotiable technical blockers, call them out now so we don't over-promise.

— Lauren
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
